name: Batch File Transfer
description: A pattern for scheduled or triggered bulk data exchange between systems using file-based transfers. Common in government for integrating with legacy systems, partner organisations, and statutory reporting where real-time APIs are not available or appropriate.
whenToUse: Integrating with legacy systems that only support file-based data exchange
Bulk data transfers to or from partner organisations on scheduled intervals
Statutory reporting where data must be submitted in prescribed file formats
ETL processes that extract, transform, and load data between systems in batch
Scenarios where the source system cannot support real-time API integration
whenNotToUse: Real-time data synchronisation requirements where latency must be sub-second
Interactive user-facing services that need immediate data availability
Small-volume data exchanges where a simple API call would suffice
Scenarios where data freshness is critical and batch delays are unacceptable
Modern system-to-system integrations where APIs are available and preferred

typicalComponents.name: Secure File Transfer
typicalComponents.purpose: Transfer files between organisations with encryption and authentication
typicalComponents.technology: SFTP, MFT (Managed File Transfer), or AWS Transfer Family

typicalComponents.name: File Processing Engine
typicalComponents.purpose: Parse, validate, transform, and route incoming files
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Step Functions, Azure Data Factory, or custom batch jobs

typicalComponents.name: Staging Storage
typicalComponents.purpose: Temporarily store files during processing with lifecycle policies
typicalComponents.technology: S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Cloud Storage

typicalComponents.name: Scheduler
typicalComponents.purpose: Trigger batch processing at defined intervals or on file arrival
typicalComponents.technology: EventBridge Scheduler, Azure Logic Apps, or Cloud Scheduler

typicalComponents.name: Error Handling and Alerting
typicalComponents.purpose: Detect processing failures and alert operations team
typicalComponents.technology: CloudWatch Alarms, Azure Monitor, or Cloud Monitoring

securityControls: Encrypt files at rest and in transit using AES-256 and TLS/SSH
Implement IP allowlisting for SFTP connections from known partner addresses
Use SSH key-based authentication rather than passwords for file transfer
Scan incoming files for malware before processing
Implement file integrity checks using checksums or digital signatures
Apply data classification labels and retention policies to transferred files
Audit log all file transfers including source, destination, size, and timestamp
resilienceConsiderations: Implement retry logic for failed file transfers with exponential backoff
Design idempotent file processing to handle duplicate deliveries safely
Store files in durable object storage before processing to prevent data loss
Implement file-level checkpointing for large batch jobs to enable restart from failure point
Monitor for missing expected files and alert when scheduled transfers do not arrive
costConsiderations: Storage costs for staging files — implement lifecycle policies to manage retention
Compute costs only incurred during batch processing windows
Data transfer costs for cross-region or cross-account file movement
Managed file transfer service licensing may apply for enterprise MFT solutions
Consider the operational cost of managing partner connectivity and credentials
operationalConsiderations: Batch processing windows must be agreed with partner organisations
File format specifications must be documented and versioned
Partner onboarding process needed for credential exchange and connectivity testing
Monitoring must detect late, missing, or malformed files
Runbooks needed for common failure scenarios (corrupt files, connectivity issues)
Capacity planning for peak batch volumes (e.g., end-of-month reporting)

services.name: AWS Transfer Family
services.purpose: Managed SFTP/FTPS service for file exchange

services.name: Amazon S3
services.purpose: Durable file staging and archive storage

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.purpose: Event-driven file processing triggered by S3 uploads

questionsToAsk: What file formats are required by the receiving systems (CSV, XML, JSON, fixed-width)?
What is the expected file size and volume per batch window?
What are the agreed transfer schedules and SLAs with partner organisations?
How should processing failures be handled — retry, alert, or quarantine?
Are there data quality validation rules that must be applied during processing?
What is the retention requirement for processed and raw files?
commonMistakes: Not implementing idempotent processing, causing duplicate records from redelivered files
Using FTP instead of SFTP, transmitting data unencrypted over the network
Not scanning incoming files for malware before processing
Failing to implement monitoring for missing or late file deliveries
Not versioning file format specifications, causing breakage when partners change formats
